about: Differences between code and Figma that are meant to be there. Each is left out of the parity check with its reason. The check warns when an exception is no longer needed.

items.axis Callout.live: How a screen reader announces the callout. Behaviour, not appearance, so Figma has nothing to draw.
items.axis Card.padding: A boolean prop in code, drawn as an on and off variant because padding changes the frame, which a Figma boolean cannot.
items.axis Checkbox.selection: Checked, unchecked and indeterminate are the input's value in code and variants in Figma, so every look exists.
items.axis EmptyState.live: How a screen reader announces the empty state. Behaviour, not appearance, so Figma has nothing to draw.
items.axis Radio.selection: Selected is the input's value in code and a variant in Figma, so both looks exist.
items.axis Select option.content: A part of Select, see the component entry.
items.axis Select.value: Placeholder or a chosen value follows from the data in code; Figma draws both.
items.axis Tab.appearance: A part of Tabs, see the component entry.
items.axis Tab.size: A part of Tabs, see the component entry.
items.axis Toggle.checked: On and off are the input's value in code and a variant in Figma, so both looks exist.
items.component Radio: A construction part: one radio, drawn as its own set so a group can be composed. In code it is internal to RadioGroup, whose folder is Radio.
items.component Select option: A construction part: the options panel row, internal to Select in code and drawn as its own set so the panel can be composed.
items.component Tab: A construction part: one tab, internal to Tabs in code and drawn as its own set so a tablist can be composed.
items.states Modal: The hover and focus rules style the close button inside the dialog; Figma draws the dialog at rest and the button is an IconButton, compared on its own.
items.states Select option: A part of Select, see the component entry.
items.states Tab: A part of Tabs, see the component entry. The tab states are drawn here rather than on Tabs.
items.states Tabs: Tabs' states are a tab's, drawn on the Tab part.
items.states Toast: The hover and focus rules style the close and action buttons inside the toast; Figma draws the toast at rest.
